title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 276 (Removal and replacement of liquidator)

content.overview: The Tribunal may remove a company liquidator for misconduct, fraud, misfeasance, professional incompetence, or failure to exercise due care, and appoint another.
content.glance: The Tribunal may remove a company liquidator for misconduct, fraud, misfeasance, professional incompetence, or failure to exercise due care, and appoint another.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 276 (Removal and replacement of liquidator). The Tribunal may remove a company liquidator for misconduct, fraud, misfeasance, professional incompetence, or failure to exercise due care, and appoint another. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Tribunal may remove a company liquidator for misconduct, fraud, misfeasance, professional incompetence, or failure to exercise due care, and appoint another.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The liquidator is given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. A transfer of cases follows the order. The section is the control on the office, not a ground of winding up.
